rules.rationale: Main-group halides are maximally ionic with closed-shell cations; no d-states in gap, giving the widest experimental gaps.
Strong ionicity and deep O 2p valence band place oxides high on the electronegativity-difference gap ladder.
Partially filled d bands introduce states near the Fermi level, narrowing or closing gaps.
Polarizable S/Se/Te p-states raise the valence band and shrink gaps; the largest anion population needs an explicit penalty.

rules.rationale: Halides had the most negative source refractive-index effect; low polarizability inverts to wide experimental band gaps via Moss.
Largest source refractive-index effect; covalent metalloid networks are classic narrow-gap semiconductors under Moss inversion.
High mean-Z boosted source refractive index; diffuse heavy-atom orbitals increase bandwidth and reduce band gap.
Independent ionicity support: deep O 2p valence band and large electronegativity difference favor wide gaps.

skill.hypothesis: Counter-hypothesis blending Moss-inverted source penalties on metalloids and heavy-Z with domain ionicity rewards, dropping the low-confidence chalcogenide inversion. Fails where high index and wide gap coexist in ionic heavy oxides, or low source confidence misleads inversion.
